Ok, now the real work starts:

We are back on the main branch, now I want the team to work on the global definition of the detector:
- the project coordinator oversees this
- the system architect gathers information from the sub system agents that argue for the global envelopes 
- the sw engineer researches a first round of tools they would need or write in order to validate these choices (hermeticity, layer/hit per particle studies, first crude material estimates)
- the physicist researches and gives input to so far literature/historically motivated main parameters for the sub detectors, or by giving physics informated arguments e.g. for shower containmnent, etc.

Mind, in this round we are looking only for the global setup of the system, the envelopes and the interfaces.

As an outcome, there should be a PR summarizing these main considerations, an envelope definition (with a rz-drawing) and a list of follow-up questions. The MD for the pr can also be seen as the first proposal and the sign-off of this proposal or discussions about it on the PR should shape it further.

What sort of access authorizations do you think you need for this ?
- web search (ok)
- pip installation (in sandbox ok)

The access you’ve authorized is enough to start: web research and sandbox-local Python installs, plus the Git branch, commits, push and PR creation implied by your request. I’ll use the existing ODD checkout and literature cache. If a required source needs institutional access or a tool needs permissions beyond those, I’ll flag the specific blocker.

I’ll coordinate subsystem envelope proposals, an independent physics review and a software validation plan, then combine them into a draft global-layout proposal with an r–z drawing and open questions. This round will stay at envelopes and interfaces; the PR will be the place to discuss and refine the proposal before sign-off.

The subsystem review has already found two important interface constraints: ODD leaves only 20 mm between the outer tracker allocation and the solenoid, and 50 mm before the ECal endcap. Those are nominal spaces, not demonstrated room for services or timing.

The muon team has also resolved the endcap coordinates from the factories: the outer allocation reaches |z| = 10.27 m. The proposal will distinguish these allocated volumes from active coverage and expected hit counts.

The System Architect’s first candidate keeps ODD’s overall ordering and scale, but reserves more space around the tracker and calorimeters. It moves the muon barrel’s inner boundary outward to accommodate that expansion.

These are proposed space allocations for discussion, not engineering-validated dimensions. The physics reviewer is checking their coverage implications and keeping the main choices explicit: calorimeter depth, forward acceptance, and whether muons need independent momentum measurement or tracker-assisted identification.

The draft now has a concrete envelope and an r–z drawing. The first checks highlight a key decision: retaining ODD’s forward apertures gives calorimeter entrance coverage near |η| ≈ 3.1, which does not match a possible tracker ambition of |η| = 4. I’m documenting that mismatch and the unresolved magnet, services, and muon requirements explicitly in the proposal.

The subsystem inputs are complete. I’m consolidating them into a draft design and preparing the PR for review. The main open choices are coil placement, forward coverage, timing space, and the muon system’s role. The drawing and diagnostic script are reproducible; their results describe allocated space, not sensitive-layer counts or shower containment.

The proposal is ready for publication. All eight envelope-tool tests pass, and the diagnostic finds no overlapping allocation rectangles. It also makes the forward gap concrete: at η = 3.5 a ray misses ECal and only grazes HCal; at η = 4 it intersects only the tracker allocation. These findings are recorded as questions for review, not performance claims.

[PR #4 is open](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/4) with the envelope table, r–z drawing, six specialist inputs, validation-tool plan, and prioritized review questions. I’m recording the publication in the Git session log; DES-003 and ADR-006 remain drafts for human discussion and sign-off.

Created [PR #4 — Global detector envelopes and interfaces](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/4).

Includes:

- **DES-003 / ADR-006** draft proposal and six specialist inputs.
- Numerical envelopes and reproducible **r–z drawing**.
- Interface ownership, physics rationale, validation-tool plan and follow-up questions.
- Source provenance and curated session log.

**Checks:** 34 tests passed; 22 session records validated. No detector simulation performed.

Main review decisions: coil placement, forward coverage, timing allocation, services/material accounting, and muon role. Human sign-off remains pending.

Branch: `design/global-envelopes`; working tree clean. No additional authorization needed.
